android.desc:
A coloring book app that is only a coloring app, made by a dad who wanted one he didn't have to supervise.

I made JustColor for my own son. I wanted something he could open by himself, with nothing in it I would have to watch him around.

No ads. Nothing to buy inside. No grown-up area, no accounts, no sign-up, and no internet at all - totally offline and available fully in airplane mode, in the car, or anywhere without Wi-Fi.

The app is priced to cover the fees to be listed on both app stores and to pay artists to source more images.

Every button is a picture, so toddlers and preschoolers who cannot read yet manage on their own. Tap an area to fill it, or draw freehand with chunky crayons. Taps are forgiving, so a small finger that lands just next to a shape still fills it. There are 30+ crayons including skin tones, soft pastels, patterns and glitter.

The coloring pages include Australian animals like koalas, kangaroos and wombats, dinosaurs, fire trucks, trains and tractors, octopuses and sea turtles, puppies, kittens and bunnies, farm animals, safari animals, pirates, rockets and astronauts, diggers, friendly monsters, Halloween, summer and back to school I'm constantly looking out for more images, and new pages arrive as free updates.

Pictures save themselves as your child goes. A favorite page can be colored again and again, and every version is kept side by side, so they can choose the one they like best.

Works on phones and tablets.

quotes.text:
Hi folks,

I'm a dad of 2 kids and I got frustrated by the way apps for small kids are designed. Signups, ads, videos, coins, rewards etc. So annoying. I can't just hand the device to my kids when I need a break or use it with little/no connectivity when we travel.

I made a really simple coloring app that has none of that.
And it's not "trust me I'm not capturing data", it's "the app doesn't request permission to access internet".

Sure, the business model isn't there: the app can't ask for reviews, I don't know which designs work best, I don't have analytics, but as a parent, that's what I actually wanted.

I think it's priced fairly given my aim is to cover the fees to be on both stores and to pay artists to get more designs to color. However, if you don't feel like paying or you can't pay, no problem, there are some codes to get it for free.

https://justcolor.yellowbits.net/

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.justcolor.app

A better way for kids apps is possible

If you download it and you like it, I'd appreciate a review on the store
